title: The Good and the Bad Figs

questions.question: What king of Babylon had taken Jehoiachin the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile when the Lord showed Jeremiah the vision in chapter 24?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:1 (ESV): "After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken into exile from Jerusalem Jeconiah (Jehoiachin),"

questions.question: What did the Lord show Jeremiah placed before the temple of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:1 (ESV): "the Lord showed me this vision: behold, two baskets of figs placed before the temple of the Lord."

questions.question: Describe the contents of the two baskets of figs.
options: One very good, the other very bad
questions.correctAnswer: One very good, the other very bad
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:2 (ESV): "One basket had very good figs, like first-ripe figs, but the other basket had very bad figs, so bad that they could not be eaten."

questions.question: What did the Lord ask Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:3 (ESV): "And the Lord said to me, 'What do you see, Jeremiah?'"

questions.question: Whom do the very good figs represent?
options: The exiles from Judah whom God sent away to Chaldea for their good
The priests serving in the temple
The righteous kings of the past
questions.correctAnswer: The exiles from Judah whom God sent away to Chaldea for their good
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:5 (ESV): "Like these good figs, so I will regard as good the exiles from Judah, whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans."

questions.question: "I will set my eyes on them for..., and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up, and not tear them down; I will plant them, and not pluck them up."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:6 (ESV): "I will set my eyes on them for good, and I will bring them back to this land."

questions.question: "I will give them a heart to know that I am the Lord, and they shall be my people and I will be their God, for they shall... to me with their whole heart."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:7 (ESV): "for they shall return to me with their whole heart."

questions.question: Whom do the very bad figs represent?
options: Zedekiah and the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those in Egypt
The people of Edom and Moab
questions.correctAnswer: Zedekiah and the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those in Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:8 (ESV): "Like the bad figs that are so bad they cannot be eaten... so will I treat Zedekiah the king of Judah, his officials, the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those who dwell in the land of Egypt."

questions.question: "I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, to be a reproach, a... , a taunt, and a curse in all the places where I shall drive them."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:9 (ESV): "to be a reproach, a byword, a taunt, and a curse in all the places where I shall drive them."

questions.question: "And I will send... , famine, and... among them, until they shall be utterly destroyed from the land that I gave to them and their fathers."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:10 (ESV): "And I will send sword, famine, and pestilence among them,"

questions.question: Who was taken into exile along with Jehoiachin according to Jeremiah 24:1?
options: The officials of Judah, the craftsmen, and the metal workers
questions.correctAnswer: The officials of Judah, the craftsmen, and the metal workers
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:1 (ESV): "After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken into exile from Jerusalem Jeconiah... together with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen, and the metal workers,"

questions.question: How did the bad figs taste?
options: So bad that they could not be eaten
They tasted fine but look terrible
questions.correctAnswer: So bad that they could not be eaten
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:2 (ESV): "but the other basket had very bad figs, so bad that they could not be eaten."

questions.question: To where did the Lord say some of the remnant (the bad figs) would mistakenly dwell, leading to their destruction?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:8 (ESV): "the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those who dwell in the land of Egypt."

questions.question: The Lord will give the good exiles a heart to know what?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:7 (ESV): "I will give them a heart to know that I am the Lord,"

questions.question: What is the promise of relation between God and the good exiles?
options: They shall be my people and I will be their God
They shall rule over the Babylonians
They will never see famine again
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be my people and I will be their God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 24:7 (ESV): "and they shall be my people and I will be their God,"

key_verse_text: I will give them a heart to know that I am the Lord, and they shall be my people and I will be their God, for they shall return to me with their whole heart.
